purpose: Reconcile the locally present hydrogen-refueling-station measurements with the privacy-bounded validation roles already exposed to the model.

collections_screened: local project data and cached public validation material
local_search.interpretation: The local measured HRS corpus is quantitatively substantial. The count is the curated privacy-bounded bundle used by the existing station-side evidence records; raw paths, names and rows remain outside the repository.

semantic_limits: flow unit and reference basis are not independently attested
no vehicle or receptacle boundary is present
no synchronized dispenser or vehicle event
temperature unit and sensor-role mapping require custodian attestation before parameter fitting

measured_collections.validated_boundary: station-equipment pressure, temperature and state transitions
semantic_limits: flow units and state semantics are not fully attested
vehicle/dispenser candidate count is zero in the expanded header screen

missing_for_full_loop: delivered mass or attested mass-flow channel
common time base and initial conditions
controller/protocol/ESD state aligned to the same event
coverage_assessment.main_limit: The local corpus is rich for station-side dynamics and equipment-state validation, but it is not a single independently scorable station-to-vehicle refueling cohort.

recommended_next_use: Use the pressure and lifecycle bundles for chronological station-side calibration and holdouts behind an explicit controlled-data profile.
Use the wide equipment bundle to validate compressor, cooling, valve and ESD state transitions before any vehicle-side claim.
Keep flow scale, temperature roles and state semantics behind custodian attestation gates.
Combine this station-side evidence with public tank, refueling, release, fire, dispersion and detector data only as component-level validation.
Keep the full-loop external-validation gate closed until a deidentified synchronized vehicle/receptacle cohort is approved.
claim_boundary: Local HRS data are abundant and actionable for station-side and equipment-boundary validation. They do not by themselves validate vehicle SOC, delivered mass, dispenser protocol compliance, or site-specific consequence distances.
